subject: Science
title: Seeing and hearing
objectives: Children will use their eyes to find, match and name objects.
Children will use their ears to find and name sounds.
content: Using eyes to find, match and name objects, using ears to find and name sounds, and playing spot and guess games.
teachingActivities: Ask children to look and listen slowly; give time; use real objects and everyday sounds; never test with loud sounds.
learnerActivities: Use eyes to find hidden objects and ears to name sounds.
resources: A bell, a rattle and a spoon with a cup
assessment: Observe whether each child finds a hidden object by looking and names a sound by listening.
expectedOutcomes: Finds a hidden object by looking.
Names a sound heard in the room.

lessons.title: Looking with my eyes
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will use their eyes to find and name objects.
successCriteria: Says the name of what they see
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name main body parts including eyes and ears.
resources: A tray of five familiar objects
lessons.starter: Point to your eyes and say "We see with our eyes." Look around the room and say "I see a door."
teacherActivities: Show the tray and name each object slowly.
Cover the tray and take one object away, then show it again. Ask "What is missing?"
Let each child choose an object and tell what they see.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the names.
Child looks and points to the ball.
Child looks and says or points.
Child picks and names it.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the tray and name each object slowly. Children: Children look and say the names.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Find the ball" and wait. Children: Child looks and points to the ball.
Step 3. Teacher: Cover the tray and take one object away, then show it again. Ask "What is missing?" Children: Child looks and says or points.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose an object and tell what they see. Children: Child picks and names it.

practical.title: What do I see?
steps: Place five objects on a tray.
Ask each child to find a named object.
Take one away and ask what is missing.
practical.safety: Use large safe objects only. Keep the tray at child height and supervise handling.

differentiation.support: Use three objects and point to help.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find two objects in one go.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Cover the tray and say "Thank you, eyes."
lessons.homeConnection: Play I spy with your child at home and name what you see.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use their eyes to find and name objects" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: I see with my eyes. What do I see?

lessons.title: Spot the hidden picture
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will find hidden pictures around the room using their eyes.
successCriteria: Says what is on the picture
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name main body parts including eyes and ears.
resources: Six picture cards hidden around the room
lessons.starter: Say "Some pictures are hiding. Use your eyes to find them." Show one picture so children know what to find.
teacherActivities: Show the six picture cards and name each one.
Hide the pictures in easy, low places.
Say "Look, look, look" and let children search.
Put the pictures in the basket and name each one.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the names.
Children watch where you hide them.
Children look and find pictures.
Child brings a picture and names it.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the six picture cards and name each one. Children: Children look and say the names.
Step 2. Teacher: Hide the pictures in easy, low places. Children: Children watch where you hide them.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Look, look, look" and let children search. Children: Children look and find pictures.
Step 4. Teacher: Put the pictures in the basket and name each one. Children: Child brings a picture and names it.

practical.title: Hide and find
steps: Hide six pictures in easy places.
Bring the picture to the basket and name it.
practical.safety: Hide pictures only in clear, low places away from hazards. Supervise the search and keep children together.

differentiation.support: Walk with the child and point to the area.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to hide a picture for a friend to find.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Count the pictures in the basket and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Hide a small toy at home and let your child find it using their eyes.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find hidden pictures around the room using their eyes" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Listening with my ears
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will use their ears to name sounds.
successCriteria: Names or points to a sound source
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name main body parts including eyes and ears.
resources: A bell, a rattle and a spoon with a cup
lessons.starter: Point to your ears and say "We hear with our ears. Shh, listen." Ring the bell.
teacherActivities: Show each sound-maker and make its sound.
Hide behind a screen and make a sound.
Say "What can you hear?" and wait in silence for ten seconds.
Let each child make a sound for friends to name.
learnerActivities: Children listen and name each object.
Children listen and point to the object.
Children listen and say or point.
Child makes a sound and friends name it.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each sound-maker and make its sound. Children: Children listen and name each object.
Step 2. Teacher: Hide behind a screen and make a sound. Children: Children listen and point to the object.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "What can you hear?" and wait in silence for ten seconds. Children: Children listen and say or point.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child make a sound for friends to name. Children: Child makes a sound and friends name it.

practical.title: Listening game
steps: Put three sound-makers on the mat.
Hide behind a screen and make one sound.
Children point to the matching object.
practical.safety: Use gentle sounds only. Do not use very loud sounds near children’s ears.

differentiation.support: Offer two sound-makers and make the sound twice.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to close their eyes and name the sound.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Cover the sound-makers and say "Thank you, ears."
lessons.homeConnection: Listen for sounds at home and name them with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use their ears to name sounds" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Mystery sound bag
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will guess an object by its sound.
successCriteria: Guesses what is in the bag by listening
Says the name of the object
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name main body parts including eyes and ears.
resources: A bell, a spoon, a small shaker and a key ring
lessons.starter: Shake the bag gently and say "What is in my bag? Listen."
teacherActivities: Put the bell in the bag, shake it and ask "What is it?"
Take it out to show them.
Repeat with the spoon, shaker and key ring.
Let each child shake the bag and ask the group.
learnerActivities: Children listen and guess.
Children look and check.
Children listen and guess each one.
Child shakes and friends guess.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put the bell in the bag, shake it and ask "What is it?" Children: Children listen and guess.
Step 2. Teacher: Take it out to show them. Children: Children look and check.
Step 3. Teacher: Repeat with the spoon, shaker and key ring. Children: Children listen and guess each one.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child shake the bag and ask the group. Children: Child shakes and friends guess.

practical.title: Mystery bag
steps: Put one object in a bag.
Shake the bag and ask what it is.
practical.safety: Use only large soft objects and never put anything in the mouth. Supervise the bag handling.

differentiation.support: Offer two objects and say the names.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to put an object in the bag for a friend to guess.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Guesses an object by its sound
lessons.conclusion: Put the objects away and say thank you.
lessons.homeConnection: Play guess the sound with a cup and spoon at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "guess an object by its sound" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 2 senses check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child uses eyes and ears to explore.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name main body parts including eyes and ears.
lessons.starter: Say "Eyes and ears" and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: spot, listen and mystery bag.
At each station ask "What do you see?" or "What do you hear?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child answers with a word or gesture.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: spot, listen and mystery bag. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What do you see?" or "What do you hear?" Children: Child answers with a word or gesture.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Eyes and ears stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use gentle sounds.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two choices.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to run a listening game.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: finds an object by looking; names a sound by listening; says which body part is used.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 2
Uses eyes and ears to explore
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye with eyes and ears.
lessons.homeConnection: Play look and listen games at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child uses eyes and ears to explore" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
